pr_body:
Prior to this PR, the last line in the bash script below would find that the server had crashed with

> wall time X is not allowed to be greater than upper bound of Y.

The reason is that upon the second start, the node would persist a "temporary" `now()+5s` upper bound but then fail to update it.

This PR ensures that the update loop starts unconditionally and maintains (i.e. either updates or erases) the HLC upper bound. This likely fixes other crashes of the same sort when the cluster setting is changed while a node is going down (in which case it's conceivable that a node would boot with a persisted upper bound but without a desire to keep maintaining time timestamp).

```

roachprod wipe local
roachprod start local:1
roachprod sql local:1 -- -e "SET CLUSTER SETTING server.clock.persist_upper_bound_interval = '500ms'"
sleep 5
roachprod stop local:1
roachprod start local:1
sleep 10
roachprod sql local:1 -- -e "SELECT 1"
```

With the fix, after restarting, the server logs

> persisting HLC upper bound is enabled [every 0.50s]

a second time (the first time being when the setting is set). Without the fix, we see this log line only once, not to mention the crash.

Fixes #137331.

Epic: none
Release note (bug fix): a problem was fixed which could cause nodes running under the `server.clock.persist_upper_bound_interval` cluster setting to crash after restarts with error "wall time <timestamp> is not allowed to be greater than upper bound of <timestamp>". This problem would occur frequently in single-node clusters, but can not be ruled out on multi-node clusters. It is now fixed in both.

[This test on roachdash](https://roachdash.crdb.dev/?filter=status:open%20t:.*clock/monotonic/persistent.*&sort=title+created&display=lastcommented+project) | [Improve this report!](https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/tree/master/pkg/cmd/bazci/githubpost/issues) Interesting failure. It seems that the problem here is not in what the test is aiming to exercise. Let's recap the test first. This single-node test starts the node to set up the `server.clock.persist_upper_bound_interval` setting, then shuts down the node again once an upper bound has been persisted. It then winds the clock back by a minute, starts the node again, and makes sure the database reports a time that did not regress (because the node is supposed to realize that it persisted a far future timestamp before it shut down, and will sleep until that timestamp is in the past; the logs show that this is also happening, as desired). Then it shuts down the node, fixes the clock, and starts it again. In fact, everything works great! When the node comes up with the bad clock, it sleeps until its previously persisted high water mark, the test is happy, and so on. But when the test restores the clock and restarts the node, five seconds in the node crashes: > wall time 1735898192649846960 [09:56:32] is not allowed to be greater than upper bound of 1735898192649128040. These timestamps both reflect the "correct" time at which the node came back up, i.e. this has nothing to (as far as I can tell) with the fact that in the previous life of the process, the clock had been rewound. Concretely: The offending timestamp 1735898192649846960 is 09:56:32.649 plus 718.92µs The persisted high water mark is 1735898192649128040 is 09:56:32.649 The log file of this crashing process begins at (correct) timestamp 09:56:27.495186. The node crashes at 09:56:32 (the timestamps above). I'm pretty sure the reason it crashes ~5s after start is because of this code: [/pkg/server/clock_monotonicity.go#L249-L260](https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/47699f3887ad5d1b8c7c5905eb5c49628aa59bbe/pkg/server/clock_monotonicity.go#L249-L260) ```go if hlcUpperBoundExists { // The feature to persist upper bounds to wall times is enabled. // Persist a new upper bound to continue guaranteeing monotonicity // Going forward the goroutine launched below will take over persisting // the upper bound if err := s.clock.RefreshHLCUpperBound( persistHLCUpperBoundFn, int64(5*time.Second), ); err != nil { return errors.Wrap(err, "refreshing HLC upper bound") } } ``` Basically, if the node is restarting with a known upper bound (as is the case here), it writes a temporary new upper bound of `now()+5s`, which comes out to the high water mark we see in the crash. But then it is supposed to start a goroutine that updates this high water mark. With the cluster setting we still have set, this should occur every 500ms, and should clobber this initial `now()+5s` value. In other words, 500ms after ~09:28, we should have updated the upper bound to now()+3*500ms, and keep doing this twice per second in this code below: [/pkg/server/clock_monotonicity.go#L262-L276](https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/47699f3887ad5d1b8c7c5905eb5c49628aa59bbe/pkg/server/clock_monotonicity.go#L262-L276) ```go _ = s.stopper.RunAsyncTask( ctx, "persist-hlc-upper-bound", func(context.Context) { periodicallyPersistHLCUpperBound( s.clock, persistHLCUpperBoundIntervalCh, persistHLCUpperBoundFn, tickerFn, s.stopper.ShouldQuiesce(), nil, /* tick callback */ ) }, ) return nil ``` But I think what we're seeing is a case where we write this first high water mark but then **fail** to maintain it. There is strong evidence to this end, namely that we never hit this logging: [/pkg/server/clock_monotonicity.go#L199-L208](https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/47699f3887ad5d1b8c7c5905eb5c49628aa59bbe/pkg/server/clock_monotonicity.go#L199-L208) ```go log.Ops.Info(context.Background(), "persisting HLC upper bound is enabled") } else { if err := clock.ResetHLCUpperBound(persistHLCUpperBoundFn); err != nil { log.Ops.Fatalf( context.Background(), "error resetting hlc upper bound: %v", err, ) } log.Ops.Info(context.Background(), "persisting HLC upper bound is disabled") ``` except when the cluster setting is first set. The way the code is written is that the loop is reactive to the cluster setting getting updated. The code seems to assume that when you set a callback, you get notified anyway - maybe this isn't the case, i.e. the code fails to realize we're starting up with the cluster setting already active, and perhaps a single-node cluster as we have here is an edge case. Sadly I can't see the goroutine in the stack traces. I think this is because the node started to shut down by the time the trace was collected and so the maintenance goroutine had already terminated. But I should be able to reproduce locally that in the scenario of the test, we fail to maintain the high water mark even though we should, and the crash should actually reproduce. Fix PR https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pull/139120. Not release blocker - this must have been around for ages. Not sure why it's failing only now. Actually let me flag this as GA-blocker. _If_ you hit that problem, it's pretty bad because nodes crash. Based on the specified backports for linked PR #139120, I applied the following new label(s) to this issue: branch-release-24.3. Please adjust the labels as needed to match the branches actually affected by this issue, including adding any known older branches. :owl: Hoot!
